inspection_summary: Inspected all 2,408 Python splitlines of the normalized 34-page article. The source develops an unconditional smoothed explicit-formula factorization of zeta into complementary prime and zero factors, uses it to separate arithmetic and random-matrix contributions to critical-line moments, and rigorously verifies the proposed split for k=1 and k=2. The prose and proof architecture are recoverable, while many displayed formulas require formula-aware checking and the appendix plots are not recoverable from the text layer alone.

sections_inspected.label: Title, abstract, and publication front matter
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: States the prime-times-zero approximation and moment-model program; otherwise front matter.

sections_inspected.label: 1. Introduction
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Motivates moment constants, diagnoses the prime-free random-matrix model, states the hybrid product, splitting conjecture, prime-factor moment theorem, zero-factor conjecture, and verified k=1,2 cases.

sections_inspected.label: 2. The Proof of Theorem 1
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Derives the hybrid Euler-Hadamard product from a smoothed explicit formula and controls smoothing, pole, trivial-zero, truncation, and zero-limit effects.

sections_inspected.label: 3. The Proof of Theorem 2
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Replaces the exponential prime factor by a corrected Euler product, truncates its Dirichlet series, applies a mean-value theorem, and extracts arithmetic and scale factors.

sections_inspected.label: 4. Support for Conjecture 3
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Models the local zero factor by periodicized unitary eigenangles and evaluates its moment through Toeplitz/Fisher-Hartwig asymptotics.

sections_inspected.label: 5. The Proof of Theorem 3, k=1
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Combines a truncated reciprocal Euler product with a twisted zeta second moment, gcd reorganization, and Euler factors to prove the split for k=1.

sections_inspected.label: 5. The Proof of Theorem 3, k=2
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Uses a fourth-moment-with-Dirichlet-polynomial formula and detailed multiplicative analysis of diagonal and off-diagonal terms to prove the split for k=2.

sections_inspected.label: Appendix A. Graphs
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Describes a pointwise numerical illustration of complementary X-dependence; the normalized text preserves prose and captions but not the plotted curves.

accepted_units.title: Random-matrix universality lacks the arithmetic factor
accepted_units.why_material: Explains why characteristic polynomials recover the universal moment factor yet omit primes, motivating an explicit-formula model that contains both zeros and arithmetic.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the matrix-size scaling, moment asymptotic, identification of the universal constant, the missing-factor diagnosis, and the proposed remedy.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-sensitive for the moment constants; the conceptual contrast is prose-grounded.

accepted_units.title: Unconditional hybrid Euler-Hadamard factorization
accepted_units.why_material: States the central decomposition zeta=PX ZX times controlled errors, with the smoothing kernel, prime factor, zero factor, and weighted-prime variant made explicit.
accepted_units.context_note: Retains all hypotheses, definitions, error terms, and the remark distinguishing the sharp and weighted prime factors.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Strongly formula-dependent; displayed definitions and error exponents should be checked against the retained PDF before downstream symbolic use.

accepted_units.title: The scale X transfers resolution between primes and zeros
accepted_units.why_material: Interprets the factorization as complementary truncated Euler and Hadamard products and shows how X trades the number of local zeros against included primes.
accepted_units.context_note: The RH assumption here is explicitly temporary and explanatory; the preceding theorem itself is unconditional.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The qualitative tradeoff is prose-grounded; the local product display is formula-sensitive.

accepted_units.title: Moment splitting into prime and zero factors
accepted_units.why_material: Introduces the pivotal independence-style hypothesis that the moment of the hybrid product asymptotically factors into separate moments.
accepted_units.context_note: Preserves the X range and k restriction; this is conjectural at this point, not a consequence of Theorem 1 alone.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-dependent for normalization and parameter range.

accepted_units.title: Prime-factor moments separate arithmetic and scale terms
accepted_units.why_material: Gives a rigorous moment asymptotic for PX in which a(k,sigma) carries prime arithmetic and FX carries the critical-line scale transition.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes uniformity in sigma and the special identification a(k,1/2)=a(k).
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Strongly formula-dependent, especially the Euler product and the piecewise FX definition.

accepted_units.title: Local zero statistics determine the zero-factor moment
accepted_units.why_material: Matches zero spacing to unitary eigenangle spacing, states the ZX moment conjecture, identifies effective degree log T/(e^gamma log X), and shows the X factors cancel when combined with PX.
accepted_units.context_note: Separates the random-matrix heuristic from the rigorous prime-factor theorem and records uncertainty about the maximal X range.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-sensitive for the Barnes-G constant and scaling; modeling claims are explicitly heuristic.

accepted_units.title: The split and zero-factor conjecture hold for k=1 and k=2
accepted_units.why_material: States the inverse-prime-factor moment theorem and its consequences: rigorous verification of both conjectural components in the first two cases.
accepted_units.context_note: Uses the hybrid approximation to identify zeta/PX with ZX and then combines with Theorem 2.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-dependent for the asymptotic and X range.

accepted_units.title: Extension to L-functions and lower-order terms
accepted_units.why_material: Records that the hybrid mechanism is expected to transfer to other L-functions and derivative moments while identifying lower-order terms as an unresolved test of the model.
accepted_units.context_note: These are proposed extensions, not established results in this source.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose-grounded.

accepted_units.title: Smoothing makes the explicit formula summable
accepted_units.why_material: States the smoothed logarithmic-derivative explicit formula and explains that repeated integration by parts supplies absolute convergence of the zero and trivial-zero sums.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the Mellin-transform kernel, support-induced finite prime sum, decay bound, and why smoothing is structurally required.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Strongly formula-dependent; OCR has fraction and transform-layout risk.

accepted_units.title: Horizontal integration converts the explicit formula to log zeta
accepted_units.why_material: Integrates the logarithmic derivative with a controlled logarithm branch, turning prime, zero, pole, and trivial-zero contributions into U-kernel terms for log zeta.
accepted_units.context_note: Retains the branch-cut convention and absolute-convergence justification needed for the representation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula- and branch-convention-dependent.

accepted_units.title: Concentrated kernel support yields the hybrid product with uniform errors
accepted_units.why_material: Uses support near e to quantify Mellin decay, suppress the pole and trivial zeros, and exponentiate the log formula into a weighted prime factor times the zero factor.
accepted_units.context_note: Shows how localization of the smoothing kernel directly controls the factorization error.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Strongly formula-dependent for powers of X, s, and log X.

accepted_units.title: Sharpening the weighted prime factor and extending through zeros
accepted_units.why_material: Shows that only a short terminal band of prime powers distinguishes the weighted and sharp factors, bounds that replacement, and uses the local expansion of E1 to make both sides vanish consistently at zeros.
accepted_units.context_note: Completes the proof of Theorem 1, including the formerly excluded zero locations.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-sensitive; the local asymptotic exp(-U(z))~Cz is readable from the prose.

accepted_units.title: Corrected Euler product cancels the missing prime-square terms
accepted_units.why_material: Constructs PX* so its logarithm matches PX through the relevant prime powers and exposes an exact cancellation in the transition range sqrt(X)<p<=X.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the bridge from an exponential Mangoldt sum to a tractable Euler/Dirichlet product.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Strongly formula-dependent, especially product exponents and the cancellation at j=2.

accepted_units.title: Smooth-number truncation plus a Dirichlet-polynomial mean value
accepted_units.why_material: Expands PX*^k over X-smooth numbers, controls the tail uniformly from the X-versus-log T restriction, and converts the moment into a diagonal coefficient sum via a mean-value theorem.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes coefficient domination for either sign of k, the truncation mechanism, and cross-term control.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-sensitive for the exponent bounds and uniformity conditions.

accepted_units.title: The diagonal coefficient sum isolates the arithmetic Euler product
accepted_units.why_material: Factors the diagonal sum prime by prime, shows the corrected large-prime factors are negligible, and identifies the convergent arithmetic factor a(k,sigma) times a truncated zeta product.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the proof step that separates arithmetic content from scale dependence.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Strongly formula-dependent; prime ranges and error exponents matter.

accepted_units.title: Mertens and the exponential integral unify the critical transition
accepted_units.why_material: Evaluates the truncated zeta product as either (e^gamma log X)^(k^2) on the critical line or a zeta/exponential-integral expression off it, completing Theorem 2.
accepted_units.context_note: The prime-number-theorem calculation makes the piecewise FX factor conceptually continuous across regimes.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-sensitive for signs, powers, and the E1 argument.

accepted_units.title: From a local zero statistic to a periodic unitary statistic
accepted_units.why_material: Rewrites |ZX| through cosine-integral contributions of nearby zeros, replaces their ordinates by unitary eigenangles, and periodicizes the local kernel so the matrix calculation is well-defined.
accepted_units.context_note: The RH and random-matrix substitutions are explicit assumptions; nonzero periodic images are later bounded.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-dependent and heuristic; the locality claim is also stated in prose.

accepted_units.title: Effective matrix dimension is fixed by rescaled local density
accepted_units.why_material: States the random-matrix asymptotic and explains why rescaling eigenangles by e^gamma log X is equivalent, for local statistics, to dimension N/(e^gamma log X).
accepted_units.context_note: Connects the hybrid zero factor directly to the earlier characteristic-polynomial model through mean density.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-sensitive for the asymptotic constant; conceptual explanation is prose-grounded.

accepted_units.title: Toeplitz determinant and Fisher-Hartwig singularity extraction
accepted_units.why_material: Uses Heine's identity to turn the unitary expectation into a Toeplitz determinant, factors its zero singularity, and invokes a Fisher-Hartwig asymptotic with an explicit smooth-symbol constant.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the main bridge from a random-matrix expectation to Fourier analysis of the smoothing kernel.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Strongly formula-dependent; determinant indices and constant E require source/PDF fidelity.

accepted_units.title: Fourier data and singular value determine the Toeplitz constant
accepted_units.why_material: States the Fourier coefficients of log b and the asymptotic value b(0), then combines them to recover the Barnes-G moment constant and the scale (e^gamma log X)^(-k^2).
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the cutoff behavior of v and the harmonic-sum evaluation used in the constant.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Strongly formula-dependent.

accepted_units.title: Periodicized cosine integrals encode the cutoff in Fourier coefficients
accepted_units.why_material: Computes the Fourier coefficients of log b by cancellation between the logarithmic singular factor and a cosine-integral transform, yielding k v(exp(n/log X))/n.
accepted_units.context_note: Preserves the n=0 case and the positive-frequency calculation separately.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Strongly formula-dependent; integral identities and signs matter.

accepted_units.title: The local logarithmic singularity cancels and periodic images are negligible
accepted_units.why_material: Shows that the singular factor and j=0 cosine-integral term combine to a finite b(0), while all nonzero periodic copies contribute only O(1/log X).
accepted_units.context_note: Closes the technical gap that justified periodicizing the zero statistic.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-sensitive, but both cancellation and uniform negligibility are explicitly described.

accepted_units.title: k=1 reduces to a truncated reciprocal product and a twisted second moment
accepted_units.why_material: Expands PX*^{-1} as a short smooth-number Dirichlet polynomial and inserts it into a uniform twisted second-moment formula for zeta.
accepted_units.context_note: Retains the X restriction, coefficient behavior, truncation error, coprime formula, and aggregate error bound.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Strongly formula-dependent.

accepted_units.title: Gcd decomposition turns the k=1 diagonal into an Euler product
accepted_units.why_material: Groups coefficient pairs by their gcd, uses the divisor identity for gcd weights, extends finite smooth sums with controlled tails, and reaches a multiplicative infinite sum.
accepted_units.context_note: This unit captures the reusable diagonalization mechanism rather than each routine estimate in isolation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-sensitive for truncation powers and the squared inner sum.

accepted_units.title: Local Euler factors produce the critical normalization for k=1
accepted_units.why_material: Evaluates the multiplicative sum prime by prime, obtains 1/(e^gamma log X), and controls replacement of the truncated reciprocal product to complete the k=1 proof.
accepted_units.context_note: Separates the arithmetic local-factor calculation from the final Cauchy-Schwarz error transfer.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Strongly formula-dependent.

accepted_units.title: k=2 requires a fourth-moment Dirichlet-polynomial decomposition
accepted_units.why_material: Explains why the k=2 case uses a stronger twisted fourth-moment formula and decomposes the target into one diagonal term and two off-diagonal terms T1-T2-T3.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the cube-free coefficients, polynomial length restriction, auxiliary ranges, and coefficient weights.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Highly formula-dependent; the multi-line Gaggero formula has extraction-layout risk.

accepted_units.title: Cube-free support organizes the k=2 diagonal by square-free layers
accepted_units.why_material: Rewrites the diagonal using gcd variables, the unique g=g1 g2^2 decomposition, and coprimality constraints, then extends the remaining smooth sums to multiplicative divisor sums.
accepted_units.context_note: Shows how support restrictions convert a dense gcd expression into locally factorable data.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-sensitive; a line refers to an equation number with apparent extraction/OCR ambiguity, so exact symbolic reuse needs PDF checking.

accepted_units.title: Nested divisor sums compress to one diagonal Euler product
accepted_units.why_material: Introduces multiplicative functions A through F to evaluate nested M,N,r,s,g2 sums from the inside out and reduce S1 to independent local prime factors.
accepted_units.context_note: The named functions are temporary proof devices, not a proposed ontology.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Strongly formula-dependent; two product-index glyphs appear degraded in extraction.

accepted_units.title: Prime-range local factors yield the k=2 diagonal constant
accepted_units.why_material: Evaluates the local factors separately below and above sqrt(X), combines them with Mertens-type products, and obtains T1~(1/12)(log T/(e^gamma log X))^4.
accepted_units.context_note: Captures the origin of both the universal 1/12 and the X-dependent scale.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Highly formula-dependent; displayed algebra and prime-range boundaries require PDF fidelity.

accepted_units.title: Coprime harmonic sums supply off-diagonal local densities
accepted_units.why_material: Proves a coprime harmonic-sum estimate and iterates it to evaluate the constrained u,v sum with multiplicative density factors kappa(md)kappa(nd).
accepted_units.context_note: These lemmas isolate a reusable way to turn coprimality constraints into logarithms and local Euler corrections.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Strongly formula-dependent.

accepted_units.title: The first off-diagonal term becomes a square of a multiplicative sum
accepted_units.why_material: Applies the local-density lemma, interchanges summations, and reduces T2 to a d-sum weighted by the square of a single coefficient sum S(d).
accepted_units.context_note: This compression is the entry point for the remaining cube-free factorization.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Strongly formula-dependent.

accepted_units.title: Cube-free cancellation forces D2 to the upper-prime range
accepted_units.why_material: Factors d against the square of the primorial, shows S(d) vanishes unless its squared component uses only primes above sqrt(X), and evaluates surviving S(d) through G and H Euler factors.
accepted_units.context_note: The vanishing condition is a structural cancellation, not merely an estimate.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Highly formula-dependent; many dense divisor conditions should be scan-verified before reuse.

accepted_units.title: Multiplicative bounds make both k=2 off-diagonal terms negligible
accepted_units.why_material: Substitutes the factorized S(d), bounds the residual coprime sum and Euler products, obtains the required small bound for T2, transfers it to T3, and completes Theorem 3.
accepted_units.context_note: Makes explicit that the same mechanism controls both off-diagonal terms while T1 supplies the main term.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Highly formula-dependent.

accepted_units.title: Pointwise prime-zero compensation across two X values
accepted_units.why_material: Reports that PX and ZX change with X but their product largely cancels that dependence and closely approximates zeta near a high zero; it also defines the actual plotted sharp/unsmoothed factors.
accepted_units.context_note: The textual claim and setup are preserved, but the curves themselves are absent from the normalized text layer.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Image-dependent for independent assessment of accuracy; formulas are extraction-sensitive and the claim is only an illustration.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: A scale-mediated partition of zeta information
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Smoothing an explicit formula yields complementary prime and zero representations whose resolution is redistributed by X while their product remains zeta within controlled errors.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The sharp-factor error requires the stated intermediate regime, and formula-level reuse requires PDF verification.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Arithmetic times universal moment structure
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The prime factor supplies the arithmetic Euler product, the local zero factor supplies the Barnes-G/random-matrix term, and their X-dependent scales cancel in the zeta moment.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The general-k multiplication uses the splitting and zero-factor conjectures; this source proves only k=1 and k=2.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Smoothing as both convergence device and spectral window
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The same compactly supported kernel makes the explicit formula absolutely summable, localizes the zero contribution, and provides controlled Fourier data after periodicization.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The quantitative statements depend on this kernel class and its support near e.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Local zero density determines the effective matrix scale
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: After rescaling by e^gamma log X, the zero factor is a local statistic with the same leading asymptotics as a unitary characteristic polynomial of effective dimension log T/(e^gamma log X).
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The zeta-to-unitary substitution is heuristic even though the subsequent Toeplitz calculation is an asymptotic theorem for the matrix model.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Two levels of rigorous splitting verification
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: For k=1 and k=2, reciprocal prime factors become short smooth-number polynomials; twisted zeta moments, gcd decompositions, and local Euler-factor cancellations isolate the predicted main term and suppress off-diagonal contributions.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The k=2 machinery is substantially specialized and does not itself establish the conjecture for higher or nonintegral k.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Theoretical and pointwise X cancellation
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Changing X alters PX and ZX individually, but both the moment calculation and the reported pointwise experiment show compensating dependence in their product.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The appendix plots are unavailable in the normalized text and constitute an illustration rather than independent proof.
